title: streaming hash holds pool slot for full lifetime; shared pool docs omit hash overhead
description: crypto2dev_hash() acquires a pool slot at Init and holds it until Final (or error). The pool is shared between streaming hash and cipher operations. The sizing guidance comment at WOLFSSL_CRYPTO2DEV_POOL_SIZE says 'N concurrent AES-GCM sessions need N slots' but omits that each in-flight streaming SHA-256/384/512 also consumes one slot. A user following the guidance exactly (POOL_SIZE=N for N TLS sessions) will see WC_HW_E from cipher ops if any streaming hashes are concurrently active. Note: in TLS-safe mode (g_tls_safe_mode=1), hash returns CRYPTOCB_UNAVAILABLE immediately and does not touch the pool, so this is only a risk for non-TLS/bulk-hash users.
